note: Every reply we have received to outreach, one row each, so the reply rate is a sum rather than a feeling. Built 2026-08-22 after Hidde asked 'hou je dit bij om van te leren?' and the honest answer was that replies lived only as loose files in drafts/. Add a row the day a reply arrives; scripts/outreach_stats.py joins this with data/outreach-sent.json. CORRECTED 2026-08-23: for one day this file claimed five threads were owed a reply and all five had already been answered by Hidde himself. The reader looked in INBOX only, so his own replies were invisible. It now reads the Sent folder too and compares timestamps, because every outreach mail we send also sits in Sent and mere presence there proves nothing. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-08-23: the reader matched SENDERS only, so replies from private addresses were invisible. Four were hidden that way, including the most useful reply this project has had (Bomenstichting Amsterdam, from hhirsch@xs4all.nl). It now also matches on the SUBJECT we ourselves sent, which finds a reply from any address without opening anything else.

kinds.correction: They told us something on our pages is wrong. The most valuable kind: it fixes the product.
kinds.referral: They named the right person or desk instead. Historically our best outcome per mail.
kinds.data: They gave or offered data, photographs, permission or a source.
kinds.answer: They answered a specific question we asked.
kinds.wrong_target: The address was not the organisation we thought it was.
kinds.auto: An automatic reply: out of office, ticket desk, or a press desk's boilerplate. Not a person, but it proves the address is live and sometimes tells us when to write again.

Asked which register the Den Bosch trees came from; answered with the municipality's own 1,907-tree register.
Stood at a Den Bosch tree and could not tell which one it was. That complaint is why all eleven Den Bosch trees now carry a recognition line.

Answered after batch 002.

Four sources, including the city's own tree app: nearly 1,300 monumental trees in The Hague, where we publish five. Licence still open.

Eight points. Two were errors on our pages (the Olifantsiep truck claim, the poplar's tallest-tree crown), both fixed. Also offered her foundation's centre route data and an introduction to Hans Kaljee, the city's tree consultant.
replies.his_reply: Answered: the two corrections are live, why the site is in English (one map for as many people as possible), is she satisfied now, does she still see anything missing, and that a link on their site would help enormously. Her walking route was NOT asked for: Hidde said she had already sent it, and no PDF from her exists anywhere in our threads, so if he cannot find it either, that route is still worth one line later. replies.note: Wrote from a private xs4all address, so the sender filter never saw her: this is the reply the reader missed and Hidde caught. Draft ready and corrected by him in session; still unsent.

replies.gave: Forwarded our enquiry to Hans Erik Lund, who runs their Tree Register, and said he appreciates making Copenhagen's outstanding trees available to people who do not read Danish.

replies.org: Fundacao Mata do Bucaco (Rita Fernandes, via their biologist)
replies.gave: Their biologist confirmed all our Bucaco trees are classified of public interest, sent the information plaques and photographs by WeTransfer, and told us to REMOVE the sequoias by the Ermida de Santo Elias because nobody can walk to them. Done the same day: the trees are out, nine girths and the heights are in, three photographs live. The reply asking written permission for the plaque texts and photographs is drafted and unsent.
replies.his_reply: Answered: confirmed the sequoias are out, thanked them for the plaques and photographs, said which three pages now carry their images and asked for written permission to keep them, and asked whether the sequoias are visible from public ground so they could return as view-only.

replies.org: Woodland Trust, Ancient Tree Inventory (Kate Lewthwaite)
replies.gave: Asked three questions and said she would discuss with colleagues: what the app is, whether it is a private individual or an institution and whether it is funded, and above all HOW WE WOULD KEEP RECORDS UP TO DATE, which she names as their main reason for not sharing data externally, because trees die and photographs age. This is the 233,000-tree register and the thread has been open and unanswered for twelve days.
replies.his_reply: He answered the same evening: private individual, no institution, no funding, site live with 95 cities; he would not publish a copy of the Inventory but a selection turned into walkable clusters; and on her real objection, keeping records current, that it runs two ways, the site re-checking against their data and readers correcting what they find on the ground. Now waiting on HER: she said she would discuss it with colleagues.

replies.gave: Said they will come back to our questions. Nothing owed yet.
Forwarded the Platzspitz question to Gruen Stadt Zuerich, with us in copy. Warm, and no move needed until they answer.
Ten working days.

replies.org: Jon Pattee, Rock Creek Conservancy (second thread)
replies.gave: His Lafayette Square tip went unanswered for eleven days because his reply arrived ten minutes after ours went out. Thanked and asked which tree he means; the lead needs a name before it can be researched.

replies.org: Jon Pattee, Rock Creek Conservancy (third message)
replies.gave: On Lafayette Square: 'a small square with several old trees with lots of personality, I'm sure you'll recognize one you like very much as soon as you set foot there.' Still no name, which is what the lead needs, and he assumes we can walk there.
replies.his_reply: Explained that the site is built from the Netherlands, so nobody here can walk over and pick the tree, which is why a tip from someone on the ground is worth so much. Thanked him for both tips and left an ask he can ignore: a name on a plaque or a photograph if he ever crosses the square.

replies.gave: Forwarded our Melbourne mail internally to their Trust Trees team ('One for you'). No answer to us yet; the right desk now has it.

THE Prague tree expert answered within two days, wanting to look, but says the page will not load for him. Checked 2026-08-26: ancienttrees.app/prague serves 200 in 0.2s, so the failure is on his side (likely his webmail's link handling). The reply should give him the bare address to type.

Two points: if we send people into Artis or the Hortus for one tree anyway, the removed paid-entry trees could just as well stay listed (entry costs the same for 1 or 10 trees); and a reminder to mind photo copyright. The first point is Hidde's call: it questions the 2026-08-23 removal of five Artis/Hortus trees.

replies.org: Quercus, Nucleo Regional de Setubal (Luis Silva)
replies.gave: No tree specialists in the Setubal nucleo, but the president himself will take a look at our page as asked.

No to a link, in plain words: they cannot advertise a private initiative from their own site. But they read the pages and found a real error: since 2020 the WHOLE park needs a ticket and the free zone no longer exists, while four of our trees said the wooded area outside the Monumental Zone was free. That is the access field, the promise that decides whether an afternoon works.
replies.his_reply: Thanked them, confirmed all four trees corrected with their own sentence quoted in the data, and asked the one question they can answer in a line: they reviewed three trees and we have four, so does the mastic at the rear access off Carrer del Torrent del Remei sit inside the fence? Flagged until they answer. No second ask about the link.

replies.org: Bayerische Schloesserverwaltung (Vera Donata Wesinger, Referat G6)
replies.gave: The Englischer Garten administration forwarded our batch 004 mail to the Gartenreferentin. She OFFERS PHOTOGRAPHS of the old trees in the Englischer Garten and Schlosspark Nymphenburg in mid or late September, and corrected one line: our story said the park's protected trees are old 'because they survived', which reads as luck, while they survived because the park is a protected Gartendenkmal tended by the Schlossverwaltung for over 200 years inside a Landschaftsschutzgebiet, which held off the building interests of the growing city.
replies.his_reply: Thanked her, confirmed the correction is live and credited to her, said September is fine, and named the three of her twelve trees that have no photograph (muc_020, muc_022, muc_014). No link ask: she had already offered something concrete.

replies.gave: Confirmed all seven of our Orto botanico trees are correct and all are in the Elenco degli Alberi Monumentali d'Italia, which is itself the second source those entries wanted. Pointed at their own pages for more, and named Associazione Unusual Address, who publish a map of every monumental tree in Florence.
replies.his_reply: Thanked her and asked for one photograph: six of the seven have one, the Himalayan cedar does not. Their site carries no licence, so their images need permission, and she is the person who can give it. Unusual Address went onto the batch 007 list instead of being asked of her.

replies.org: Park Guell (Barcelona Serveis Municipals), second answer

replies.org: Cambridge University Botanic Garden (Dr Raphaella Hull)
replies.gave: Our Cambridge enquiry was passed to her, the Acting Head of Learning. She calls the project brilliant and offers to read the pages and comment, but cannot get to it soon, so she asked whether there is a deadline.
replies.his_reply: No deadline, we are working on this for months, thanks in advance. Named the three of our five Cambridge trees that stand in the Botanic Garden so her eventual read is easy. No photo ask and no link ask: she offered to comment while telling us she is busy, and a task list is how that offer gets withdrawn.

replies.gave: Confirmed our selection: 'I would think they would the ones we would include so think you are spot on.' The custodian of the ground saying our four Blarney trees are the right four, which is the second source those entries wanted.
replies.his_reply: Thanked him and asked plainly for a link. The first draft dressed the ask as a favour to the trees and Hidde struck it: 'feels a bit deceiving, just ask for help.' Recorded in drafts/HIS_VOICE.md.

replies.org: City of Sydney, Urban Forest (Karen Sweeney)
replies.gave: A clear no on licensing the Register of Significant Trees, with the reason stated: they do not want the data republished where it could later be incorporated into paid products. They propose sending people back to the City of Sydney site instead. Written into OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md so those 2,504 trees are a settled verdict rather than an open question.
replies.his_reply: Four lines: thanks, no hard feelings, and straight about the paid tier on Hidde's own instruction, that a few extras will sit behind a subscription to cover costs while the trees stay free. No price, no date. One question back: which Sydney tree should we not be missing. A first draft defended us against a charge she never made and he struck it.

replies.org: Orto botanico di Firenze (Giulia Torta), second reply
replies.gave: Sent the photograph of the monumental Cedrus deodara we asked for, with the credit line she wants verbatim: 'Sistema Museale di Ateneo, Universita degli Studi di Firenze'. It is live, vendored onto our own domain, recorded as permission rather than an open licence. All seven Orto botanico trees now carry a picture.
replies.his_reply: Reported it live with the link, said the app is coming and makes exactly this easier, and left the door open for more.

replies.org: Dias com Arvores (Paulo V. Araujo), photographs
replies.gave: Back from holiday, sent eight photographs of Porto trees by transfer with the permission in his own words, 'Use as fotos como quiser', and promised more by the end of next week. Six landed on trees and Porto went from 5 photographs to 10. His filenames carried the species AND the place, which is what made the matching readable: from the pictures alone only two of eight could be placed with confidence. Two were of trees we do not publish and went to leads.
replies.his_reply: Thanked him properly, listed what is live, passed on the filename tip since more are coming, told him the app is nearly ready and asked him to be among the first to try it, and asked whether the Bischofia he photographed deserves a place.

replies.his_reply: Thanked her, said her tips were exactly the right sources and that we already use them, and asked whether she would look at the app and test it. A drafted question about where to find the AGE of a monumental tree was cut on Hidde's call: she is the secretariat, and that question belongs to their members.

replies.org: Paulo V. Araujo (Dias com Arvores, Porto)
replies.gave: Corrected the mail we sent this morning: he photographed the Bischofia of the Jardim Botanico BECAUSE it is on our own Porto list, and linked the page to prove it.
